This is the first applicable code in order (E1 does not apply: ChatGPT use by learners is described). The abstract also reports mainly satisfaction and descriptive survey data, with no clear quantitative learning outcome or clearly described control group, but the domain failure is sufficient for exclusion.

title: Students’ voices on ChatGPT: A pilot study on academic writing enhancement
rationale: Study is a pilot online open-response questionnaire of students' perceptions of ChatGPT use in academic writing. There is no control group and no comparison design, so E3 applies. Non-STEM content (academic writing / English literature) and perception-only outcomes also fail, but E3 is the first applicable code in order that the abstract gives positive evidence for. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported because the design is clearly a single-sample survey with no comparison group.

title: ChatGPT: An ingenious predicament
rationale: The record is a narrative/opinion-style review of ChatGPT (background, history, medical applications, ethical concerns). It reports no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, no learner-facing intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol; E1 and E3 also would apply in a loose sense, but E6 is the fundamental failure.

title: Enhancing Programming Education using GPT-Based Code Review and Automatic Comment Generation
rationale: Abstract describes a GPT-4o code review system evaluated with BERT-Score semantic similarity against reference comments, not a learning outcome measured in learners. No control group comparison or learner-based quantitative outcome is described. The claim that the framework "improves code comprehension" is unsupported by any reported comparative measure. Excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design also appears non-experimental (E3/E6 possible), but E5 is the first applicable code in order given the abstract. Note: under the protocol order, E1 does not apply since the tool is learner-facing generative AI, and E2 does not apply since programming is STEM.

title: Comparing student and educator perceptions of generative artificial intelligence for teaching, learning and assessment: results from two institutional surveys
rationale: The study is a descriptive cross-sectional survey of perceptions and self-reported use of GenAI. It has no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; only perceptions and usage are reported. It is not an intervention study with learning measures, so it fails the design and outcome criteria. The first applicable code in order is E1 (no learner-facing GenAI intervention evaluated), but the clearest failure is that it is not an empirical experimental study, so E6 is assigned as the primary reason. This exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the design is a survey.

title: Immersive Virtual Learning Experiences of Senior Secondary School Students from India and Russia: A Mixed Method Study
rationale: The intervention is immersive VR (stand-alone head-mounted VR), with no indication that learners interact with a generative AI tool. The abstract only mentions generative AI as a future study direction. Also, the outcomes are experience and attitude scales (affective/perception measures), with no quantitative learning outcome and no control group described. E1 applies first as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

title: Classroom Implementation of AI ‐Assisted Fraction Instruction for Students With Mild Autism
rationale: The study is a single-group pretest-posttest design with no comparison group, which the protocol excludes under E3. The abstract also states that AI Lobe was a rule-based adaptive learning environment and not an autonomous generative AI tutor, so the intervention criterion is likely not met as well. E1 would also be arguable, but E3 is the design failure stated outright. Population (sixth graders with mild ASD), fractions domain, and pre-post achievement outcome are otherwise met or not contradicted.

title: You Got Phished! Analyzing How to Provide Useful Feedback in Anti-Phishing Training with LLM Teacher Models
rationale: Anti-phishing security awareness training is not a science, math, statistics, engineering, computer science, or programming domain. The abstract describes an analysis of LLM embeddings of student-LLM conversations and reports no control group, learning outcome statistics, or STEM content. Exclusion for E2 (non-STEM content) applies first in the code order. Note that E1/E3 would also be uncertain from the abstract alone. No verbatim quote is required beyond the domain description, so quote is null.

title: Efficacy and limitations of ChatGPT as a biostatistical problem-solving tool in medical education in Serbia: a descriptive study
rationale: The study is a descriptive evaluation of ChatGPT's performance on 10 biostatistics problems from a handbook. ChatGPT was tested directly as a standalone tool; there is no learner group and no control group without generative AI. The design is not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in order. The abstract does not give positive evidence of an E1 or E2 failure, so E3 is the cleanest code, though the design is also descriptive rather than experimental.

title: EXPLORING GITHUB COPILOT ASSISTANCE FOR WORKING WITH CLASSES IN A PROGRAMMING COURSE
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative evaluation of Copilot interactions with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of design failure (qualitative, no comparison) is present. Per the protocol, the first applicable code in order is E1 check: Copilot is learner-facing generative AI, so E1 does not apply. E2 does not apply (programming). E3 applies because there is no comparison group without generative AI. Noting that E5 and E6 would also plausibly apply; E3 is cited as the first code the abstract clearly supports given the criteria order. Decision is exclusion.

title: PROMPTING DIFFERENCE: COLLEGE STUDENTS WITH ADHD AND THEIR USE OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS IN LEARNING CONTEXTS
rationale: Qualitative honors thesis using semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. No experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The record lacks any quantitative learning measure, so E5 applies (the design also fails the comparison and design criteria, but the rule is to report the first applicable code in order; E3 precedes E5 in the list, so E3 would be the first code that applies since there is no control group without generative AI). Given the code order, E3 is the first applicable code.

title: Comparing Lecturers and Students Attitude towards the Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence Systems in Foreign Language Teaching and Learning
rationale: The study is a survey of attitudes (UTAUT-based questionnaire) comparing lecturers and students, with no learning outcome measured and no experimental or comparison-group design. Domain is foreign language learning, which is non-STEM. Excluded at abstract stage under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); the design is also a survey, which is not eligible. Exclusion uses the first applicable code in order; E2 (non-STEM) would be an earlier-listed code only if checked first, but the primary failure is the lack of a learning outcome. Note: strictly, E2 precedes E5 in the protocol's code order and applies on the abstract (foreign language teaching is non-STEM), so the code should be E2 under the first-applicable rule.

title: Transnational higher education cultures and generative AI: a nominal group study for policy development in English medium instruction
rationale: The study is a nominal group technique with expert panellists developing a policy framework. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool, there is no control group, no learning outcome is measured, and the design is not an experiment. It is not an eligible empirical learning study. Primary exclusion is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense); E1 would also apply since no learner-facing GenAI is involved, but the first applicable code in order is E1 — see note below.

title: The Role of an E-Learning Environment Based on Generative AI in Enhancing Digital Learning Capabilities among Undergraduate Students: A Qualitative Study
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative phenomenological study using 12 semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the study reports perceptions and experiences. This is not an empirical quantitative design meeting the protocol, so it is excluded. E6 (not an empirical study) is the closest code given that the design is qualitative and not a comparative experiment; the primary failing is design/comparison and outcome, but the first applicable code in order is judged here as E6 for the qualitative nature.

title: Leveraging Large Language Model for Automatic Translation of Educational Content: Exploring the Effectiveness of Curriculum-Aware Prompt Engineering
rationale: Abstract concerns LLM-based translation of assessment items compared across two prompt strategies, with expert reviews and linguistic feature comparison. This is not a learner-facing STEM learning activity, no learning outcome or learner control group is described, and the content is educational translation rather than STEM. Excluded on the first applicable code E2 (content not STEM), since the study is about translation of assessment items rather than STEM learning; the abstract gives positive evidence that the content domain is not STEM. Note that E1 could also arguably apply because the LLM is used by researchers/translators rather than learners.

title: Engineering student perceptions of generative AI use in learning trust judgment and information seeking
rationale: The abstract describes a perception/survey study of engineering students' views of generative AI. It reports perceptions, agreement levels, and usefulness ratings, with no quantitative learning measure and no control group. Positive evidence of a failed outcome criterion (perceptions only) and of a non-experimental design is present, so exclude under E5 (the first applicable code given the protocol order; design also appears not to meet the criteria). The E5 code is chosen because the abstract explicitly reports only perceptions.

title: Evaluation of the performance and temporal variability of large language models in patient education regarding pneumothorax: a seven-day analysis
rationale: The study evaluates LLM chatbot outputs about pneumothorax patient education, rated by thoracic surgeons. The content is medical/patient education, not STEM under the protocol's domain list (science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science), and health professions/patient health information falls outside the domain. There is no learner interacting with the tool as part of a learning activity, and no control group without generative AI is evident; the design is a set of repeated chatbot output evaluations. E2 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly met on abstract evidence; the abstract gives positive evidence the content is medical rather than STEM education.

title: Evaluating the Accuracy and Reliability of Large Language Models (ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini, Grok, and Le Chat) in Answering Item-Analyzed Multiple-Choice Questions on Blood Physiology
rationale: The LLMs themselves were tested on the MCQ items; learners did not interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity. Students took the MCQ test but no LLM group was compared with a non-AI control. The design is a cross-sectional evaluation of LLM accuracy, not a controlled comparison. E1 applies as the first failing code: the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

title: Academic Self-Efficacy, Online Learning Motivation, and Perceptions of ChatGPT Among Higher Education Students
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey (correlational and t-test comparisons of perceptions) with no experimental or quasi-experimental control group, so it is not an eligible design. It measures self-efficacy, motivation and perceptions only, with no quantitative learning outcome. Domain is also not clearly STEM. Coded E6 (not an empirical intervention study) as the first applicable code is not strictly matched; the closest fit is design ineligibility, which is captured by E6 as a non-experimental empirical study. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of survey design and perception-only outcomes.

title: INVESTIGATING THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON CREATIVE WRITING SKILLS AMONG UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN SIALKOT
rationale: Abstract describes a descriptive, questionnaire-only study of students' perceptions (PU/PEOU) of AI tools. No control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions only. Domain is English creative writing, which is non-STEM, so E2 could also apply, but E5 is the earliest code supported by the abstract's positive evidence (perception-only outcome). Coding E5 as the first applicable code in protocol order: E1 is not clearly failed at abstract stage, E2 is arguably met as non-STEM content, so the first clearly applicable code should be E2. Final code applied: E2 is the earliest positive failure of a criterion in order after E1 cannot be determined; see rationale.

title: Teacher-centered LLM-based multi-agent systems–towards differentiated educational worksheets
rationale: The LLM system is teacher-facing: it generates worksheets for teachers to use, and learners do not interact with it. Learner agents are simulated, not students. This fails E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI). Evaluation is automated agent assessment plus in-service teacher feedback, with no control group, no learner outcome, and no student population, so further criteria also fail. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

title: MAIN DRIVERS OF CHATGPT ADOPTION BY ROMANIAN COMPUTER SCIENCE STUDENTS
rationale: The study is a TAM survey of perceptions and behavioural intention to use ChatGPT, with no quantitative learning outcome and no control group. Outcomes are perceptions/intention only, so it fails E5. Also appears to be a survey design without comparison group (would be E3/E6 as well), but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order after E1-E4 which are met.

title: Integrating generative AI into STEM education: Insights from science and mathematics teachers
rationale: The study is a survey of in-service STEM teachers' perceptions of generative AI under TAM. It has no learner-facing intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and the population is in-service teachers, not students. Because the design is a perception survey (not an empirical experiment on learners), the first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI) — however, the cleanest first-failing criterion is the intervention: no learner interacts with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. Applying codes in order, E1 applies first.

title: The Effectiveness of a Teaching Strategy Based on Generative Artificial Intelligence in Developing Oral Communication Skills among Second-Year Middle School Students
rationale: The study targets oral communication skills taught in English language instruction, which is language learning, not STEM. Per the protocol, language learning is excluded (E2). The abstract also does not clearly state the learner's interaction with a generative AI tool, but the domain failure alone is sufficient. Population (middle school) and quasi-experimental control group with a quantitative post-test appear to be met.

title: An argumentation experience regarding concepts of calculus with ChatGPT
rationale: Abstract describes a single university student's argumentation with ChatGPT analyzed qualitatively using Toulmin's model and Habermas' rationality. No control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the design is qualitative case-style. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's quantitative sense is the closest fit; the design is qualitative/case study, which the Design row excludes). Because E6 is the first code that clearly applies on the evidence available and the protocol's design exclusion is not a separate code, the exclusion is recorded as E6 for audit review.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education: Balancing Opportunities, Risks, and Ethical Challenges in the Era of Generative AI
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It fails the eligibility criteria on design and outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, so the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type is also a review, which could alternatively be E10, but the review design is the more direct failure.

title: Enhancing Soft Skills through Generative AI in Sustainable Fashion Textile Design Education
rationale: Fashion/textile design education focused on soft skills is not a STEM domain under the protocol (science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, data science). Excluded at E2 on the abstract's positive evidence of non-STEM content. Comparison group and design are not described in the abstract, but the domain failure is sufficient.

title: Generative AI in Technology-Oriented Higher Education: A Systematized Review and Survey on Students’ Perceptions of Performance, Autonomy, and Ethical Implications
rationale: The record is a systematized literature review plus a cross-sectional anonymous survey of students. It has no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and reports perceptions and usage rather than a quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical intervention study meeting the design criteria. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly established from the abstract, and E6 (not an empirical study) is the most applicable code given the review-and-survey design. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that the design and outcome criteria fail.

title: Teachers’ Perceptions and Experiences of Using ChatGPT to Assess Students’ Scientific Epistemic Abilities
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of in-service junior high school teachers' perceptions of ChatGPT use. Generative AI is used by teachers for preparation and assessment, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity, so E1 applies (first applicable code). There is also no comparison group, no learner population, and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is a survey, which fails the design criterion as well.

title: Exploring the impact of GenAI-assisted EFL courses on foreign language anxiety and willingness to communicate: a disciplinary comparison
rationale: Study is about GenAI-assisted EFL (English as a foreign language) courses, with outcomes foreign language anxiety and willingness to communicate. Content is language learning, which the protocol explicitly excludes from the STEM domain. Accounting and electrical engineering students are the disciplinary comparison groups, but the taught content is English language, not STEM content. Exclusion code E2 applies. Affective outcomes (FLA, WTC) would also not be extracted under the protocol.

title: Assessing the effectiveness of large language models for generating and estimating time complexity of code segments
rationale: The study evaluates LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Llama) on generating and analyzing C code segments of given time complexity, with the LLM itself being the object of evaluation. There is no learner-facing intervention and no control group of learners without generative AI; the comparison is between LLMs and performance is measured on model output correctness, not on student learning. Exclusion under E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in order given the design, though E1 (not learner-facing) could also apply; the abstract shows only model-vs-model evaluation with no comparison group.

title: Using Copilot to Foster Utterance Fluency of Undergraduates: A Multiple Case Study
rationale: The content is English as a second language speaking fluency, which is language learning and not STEM (E2). The design is also a multiple case study with three participants and no comparison group, which would fail E3 and E6 if reached. E2 is the first applicable code in order.

title: Generative AI as a Catalyst for Financial Learning in Vocational Training
rationale: The abstract describes a single group measured before and after using generative AI (baseline test, then repeated test). No separate control group without generative AI is described, so E3 applies. Financial literacy is also arguably not STEM (E2 would be a secondary concern), but E3 is the first applicable code in order. Positive evidence of a within-subject pre-post design is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

title: BEYOND SKILL DEVELOPMENT: HOW GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ENHANCES TEACHERS’ SELF-EFFICACY AND ACADEMIC MOTIVATION
rationale: Participants are in-service teachers, which the protocol excludes (not K-12 or higher education students). The design is a single-group pretest-posttest (paired-samples t tests) without a non-GenAI control group, and the outcomes are self-efficacy and motivation, which are affective/perception measures rather than learning outcomes. Population exclusion (E4) is the first applicable code in order that is clearly positively evidenced.

title: The Effect of Generative AI Dependency on Academic Integrity among Postgraduate Students at KPPIM
rationale: Survey-based correlational design (regression on DAI and AIS scales) with no control group comparing generative AI use against non-AI use. Outcome is self-reported dependency and academic integrity perceptions, not a quantitative learning measure. Domain is not clearly STEM. Exclude under E3 as the first applicable code in order: no comparison group without generative AI. Note that the design and outcome also fail, but the E3 code is the first that applies in the specified order.

reason: quote not found in record; random audit sample
title: Generative AI in physics education: Approaches for instructors to integrate new tools with proven practices
rationale: The abstract describes a practice-oriented article offering strategies and guidance for instructors, connecting existing physics education research with a program guide. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Under the abstract-stage rule, this is positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so exclusion is appropriate.

title: Generative AI-assisted instruction and college students’ academic self-efficacy, computational thinking, and critical thinking disposition: A six-week pretest-posttest study
rationale: The abstract explicitly reports a one-group pretest-posttest design with no control group, which fails the comparison requirement (E3). The study is also a single-group pre-post design, which the protocol excludes. Domain is unclear from the abstract (computational thinking is mentioned, but the instructional content is not specified), but the exclusion under E3 is already decisive.

title: Assessing students’ DRIVE: A framework to evaluate learning through interactions with generative AI
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational analysis of GenAI interaction annotations against essay scores in STEM writing courses, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Its design is correlational, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion is coded E3 (no control group without generative AI), the first applicable code in the protocol's order beyond E1/E2 (E2 is unclear from the abstract alone and was not used).

title: Designing Practical Entrepreneurship: A Case Study of an Online Entrepreneurship Course for Secondary Students
rationale: The record is a design case study describing development and pilot of an entrepreneurship course, drawing on surveys, interviews and reflections. It reports no comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study. Entrepreneurship is also not clearly STEM content. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code at the abstract stage on the basis of the design-case framing; E5 and E3 would also apply. Generative AI is mentioned only as tools students negotiated, so intervention status is unclear.

title: The Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in Enhancing Self-Learning and Developing Employees’ Digital Skills: An Applied Study in the Oil Products Distribution Authority in the Middle Euphrates Region
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive analytical study using a questionnaire and interviews with employees of an oil products distribution authority. Population is workplace employees, not K-12 or higher education students (E4). The design is a survey/descriptive study with no control group, and there is no experimental learning outcome. Exclusion is based on the population criterion; the abstract gives positive evidence that the sample is employees in a workplace setting.

title: Disciplinary And Gender Differences In Students’ Perceptions of ChatGPT For Academic Assignments: A Case of Universitas Negeri Semarang
rationale: The study is a mixed-methods perception survey with interviews and no control group, and it reports only perceptions and attitudes rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Design and comparison criteria are not met on the abstract's description. Under the protocol, E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) applies as the first failing code in order (E1 and E2 are not clearly failed; E3 would also apply, but E5 is the clearest positive evidence of a non-learning-outcome design). The domain is also not clearly STEM. Excluding on E5 given the abstract's explicit description of perceptions only.

title: A Case Study of Teaching-Learning Strategies Using Generative Artificial Intelligence in a Problem-Based Learning Program for Fashion Marketing
rationale: Abstract describes a single-group design-based case study with pre-post surveys (17 of 35 students completing both), with no control group. Content is fashion marketing, which is not STEM. Exclusion is on E2 (not STEM), the first applicable code in protocol order; the abstract also gives no evidence of a comparison group (E3), and the design is a case study rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental design. No quote is strictly needed beyond the domain; the abstract's "six-week educational program" and "fashion marketing education" describe the content.

title: Exploring medical students’ intention to use of ChatGPT from a programming course: a grounded theory study in China
rationale: The study is a grounded theory qualitative design based on interviews of 30 students. It has no control group without generative AI and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion uses the first applicable code in order; E1 does not apply because ChatGPT is learner-facing, and E2 does not apply because programming is STEM. E3 is the first failing criterion in the list, since the design has no comparison group. E6 (not an empirical study) would also fit as a qualitative design, but the abstract shows empirical interview data, so E3 is the most direct code.

title: Human–AI Co-Orchestration in Data Science Education: Interactive, Adaptive, and Personalized Lecture Design for Diverse Learners
rationale: The record is an opinion article that proposes a conceptual framework and research agenda. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly established, but E6 is the decisive, first-applicable reason given the non-empirical nature of the paper.

title: Effectiveness of AI in solving math problems at the secondary school level
rationale: Abstract compares ChatGPT's accuracy against ten students' accuracy on the same 20 math questions. This is a performance comparison of AI versus humans, not a learner-facing intervention with a separate control group that does not use generative AI. No randomized or quasi-experimental comparison group is described. Positive evidence of no eligible control group, so exclude under E3 at abstract stage. Note that the code applied is E3 per the protocol's first-failing-criterion order; the intervention criterion is also doubtful (students do not interact with AI as a learning activity as described).

title: The association between generative artificial intelligence use and foreign language classroom anxiety
rationale: Abstract stage, but there is positive evidence of a failed criterion. The domain is foreign language learning (English proficiency, foreign language classroom anxiety), which is non-STEM, so E2 applies first. The design is a correlational/regression survey with no control group and no learning outcome, so it would also fail E3, E5 and E6. Only the first applicable code is reported.

title: New Technology for a New World: How AI is Creating Opportunities for Students and Faculty
rationale: The abstract describes an opinion/practice-oriented article about generative AI in community colleges. It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study that meets the protocol. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in the order used here that is supported by the abstract.

title: AS-1011-26 Resolution on Course Syllabi
rationale: The record is an Academic Senate policy resolution about the content of course syllabi, not an empirical study. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no comparison group, no design, and no learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies first in the code order that reaches a fundamental failure; E1 would also arguably apply since no learner interacts with generative AI, but the record is a policy document, so E6 is the most accurate primary code.

title: The Role of Chatgpt and Generative Artificial Intelligence in Shaping the Future of Islamic Teacher's Effectiveness in Southern Pakistan
rationale: Survey of in-service teachers about their own ChatGPT/generative AI use; learners do not interact with generative AI as part of a learning activity, and there is no control group or learning outcome. Exclusion E1 applies first (AI used by teachers, not learner-facing). Also a survey design (E6 would apply secondarily) and population is in-service teachers.

title: Preservice Teachers’ Perspective on Using Gen AI in Math Education
rationale: The study examines preservice teachers' perspectives and perceptions of GenAI tools via observations and a survey. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the outcomes are perceptions, which the protocol excludes. Design is descriptive/survey, not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison. Exclude at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the first clearly applicable code in order after intervention/domain/population checks; the comparison and design failures would also apply.

title: Redefining creativity differences for art students who use and those who do not use GenAI: evidence from network analysis
rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional network analysis comparing students who use GenAI with those who do not, based on students enrolled in art programs. Art creativity is not STEM content, so E2 applies first. There is no indication of a randomized or quasi-experimental design with an intervention and control group, and no quantitative learning outcome is evident (creativity features from network analysis). Exclusion is clear on domain at the abstract stage.

title: Experiences of nursing and medical students with the use of Artificial Intelligence tools such as ChatGPT in Uganda
rationale: The study is a qualitative descriptive design using focus groups and interviews. It has no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study that meets the protocol's design criteria, so it fails at E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative quantitative design). Exclusion is based on positive abstract evidence of a qualitative design with no control group or quantitative outcome.

title: Beyond initial adoption of generative AI: the role of AI performance and comfort expectancy in driving ChatGPT continuance among students at Indonesian universities
rationale: Survey-based cross-sectional study using PLS-SEM on continuance intention. No randomized or quasi-experimental design with a non-generative-AI control group, and no quantitative learning outcome (continuance intention is a perception/usage measure). Excluded at first applicable code E3 (no control group without generative AI). The protocol's design and outcome criteria also fail, but E3 is the first code in order that applies. Domain is not stated in the abstract, so it is not assessed as a basis for exclusion.

title: UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS' PERCEPTION ON USING CHATGPT FOR IDEA DEVELOPMENT IN ACADEMIC WRITING BASED ON TAM: A DESCRIPTIVE STUDY
rationale: placeholder

title: It Helps with Crap Lecturers and Their Low Effort: Investigating Computer Science Students’ Perceptions of Using ChatGPT for Learning
rationale: This is a mixed-methods survey study of computing students' perceptions and trust in ChatGPT. It reports no learning outcome, only perceptions and usage, and has no control group. Design is a survey, not an experiment. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome); the abstract gives positive evidence of perception-only measures. Although E3 and E6 might also apply, E5 is the first code in the protocol order that clearly fails on the abstract.

title: Supporting self-directed learning and self-assessment using TeacherGAIA, a generative AI chatbot application: Learning approaches and prompt engineering
rationale: The abstract describes design and prototyping of a generative AI chatbot with preliminary design, prompt engineering and prototyping evidence only. No controlled comparison, no learning outcome measured, and no empirical experimental design is reported. Fails design and outcome criteria on positive evidence. Intervention is generative AI and the population is K-12, but these do not rescue the exclusion. Exclusion code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first applicable in the code order given the design is a prototype without measured outcomes; E6 (not an empirical study) could also be argued, but the record describes a design/prototyping paper.

title: Generative AI ‐supported progressive prompting for professional training: Effects on learning achievement, critical thinking, and cognitive load
rationale: Participants are newly qualified nurses in professional training, not K-12 or higher education students; this is workplace/professional training. The content (ECG interpretation) is health professions education, which is also outside the STEM domain as defined by the protocol. Exclusion under E4 is the first applicable code in order (E1-E3 do not apply: a generative AI tool is learner-facing, and a conventional PP control exists; E4 precedes E2 in the code order).

title: ChatGPT in physics education: A pilot study on easy-to-implement activities
rationale: Secondary-school physics study using ChatGPT, but the only reported outcome is students' perceptions, which the protocol excludes as a non-learning outcome. No quantitative learning measure is described in the abstract. Excluded at abstract stage on E5 because positive evidence shows the outcome criterion fails.

title: Enhancing Pre-Service Teachers’ Understanding of Pedagogical Key Ideas by Integrating ChatGPT in ODL Course Tutorials
rationale: The abstract describes a case study of nine pre-service teachers with only pre/post and within-subject comparisons (Friedman test, Wilcoxon tests), and no separate control group without generative AI. This fails the comparison and design criteria (single-group pre-post, case study), so E3 applies. Domain is also unclear: pedagogical key ideas in an education course is not clearly STEM. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of no control group and a case-study design.

Coding as E6 is the first applicable code in order that the title supports; the decision is made on the title alone and should be verified by the auditor at full text if there is any doubt.

title: Pelatihan Pemanfaatan Kecerdasan Buatan (AI) dalam Pembuatan Media Promosi Kesehatan untuk Mahasiswa di Era Digital
rationale: This is a community service training report, not an empirical study. It has no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; the reported gains are descriptive (understanding, skills, awareness). Domain is health promotion media, which is not clearly STEM. Excluded at E6 as the first applicable code in the order that matters most (not an empirical study). Note that E6 is the earliest code that clearly applies; E3 and E5 would also fail.

title: What are artificial intelligence literacy and competency? A comprehensive framework to support them
rationale: The study is a conceptual framework development using iterative co-design with 30 teachers. It is not an empirical comparative study: there is no control group, no learner-facing generative AI intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the empirical study requirement (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the design is a co-design framework study rather than an experiment.

title: Performance Assessment of GPT 4.0 on the Japanese Medical Licensing Examination
rationale: The title describes GPT-4.0 performance on the Japanese Medical Licensing Examination, which is a health-professions content domain. Protocol excludes health professions education, so E2 applies. This is decided from the title alone because no abstract is indexed; the record gives no evidence of a control group or learner interaction, but the domain failure is sufficient. Note that the exam is a model-benchmark setting rather than a learner-facing study, which would also fail E1.

title: Research on the Construction and Practice of an AI-Empowered Interdisciplinary Project-Based Learning Resource System for Emerging Engineering Education
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual analysis and proposed system architecture ("this paper analyzes the internal mechanism... proposes a teaching resource system", "proposes a technical architecture"). It reports no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. The claim that the system "can promote" outcomes is not backed by reported data. This is a non-empirical paper, so E6 applies. Exclusion is supported by the abstract's description of the work as conceptual and architectural, not by a missing detail.

title: AWARENESS AND USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TOOLS BY ACADEMIC STAFF AND STUDENTS AT GBOKO POLYTECHNIC GBOKO, BENUE STATE
rationale: Descriptive survey design (no comparison group, not an experiment or quasi-experiment) and the outcome is self-reported awareness and use, not a quantitative learning measure. Abstract gives positive evidence that the design and comparison criteria fail. Per protocol exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention) and E2 (domain) are not clearly established from the abstract, so the first applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI), as the study has no control group. Note: E3 is the code specified for missing comparison; the design is survey, which the protocol also excludes under Design.

title: Uso do ChatGPT por estudantes angolanos no Instituto Superior Politécnico Privado do Uíge (ISPPU).
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive, exploratory questionnaire survey of 940 students on ChatGPT use and perceptions. There is no randomized or quasi-experimental design, no comparison group without generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome (results are usage patterns and perceptions). Positive evidence of failure on comparison, design, and outcome exists, so exclusion is warranted. E3 is the first applicable code in order that fits the lack of a control group; the survey design (E6-type) and absence of learning outcome are also failing. Domain is not stated as STEM in the abstract.

title: Framing the Role of AI Agents Through Metaphors
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative metaphor analysis (Grounded Theory) of 27 students' free associations about AI agents. It has no experimental or comparison group, no learning intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. Not an empirical study in the sense of the protocol's eligible designs; E6 is the first applicable code given the design. Note that E1 (learner-facing intervention) and the comparison requirement also fail, but E6 is applied as the most fundamental issue. Decision is clear from the abstract.

title: Using AI-Enabled Tools to Support Minority Students’ Success in HE
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative perception study of master's students using LLMs, with no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure on comparison, design, and outcome. Domain is not STEM (educational leadership and teacher education), but the abstract does not clearly establish this; E5 is the first clear failure in code order for a study with no quantitative outcome. Note E2 could also apply, but the protocol asks for the first applicable code in order, and E2 precedes E5 in order, so the stronger assignment would be E2 if the content is clearly non-STEM. The abstract shows perception-focused themes only, so E5 is applied.

title: Pedagogical conundrum, assessment anxiety, and employability dilemma: a qualitative exploration of staff perspectives on the great GenAI quandary in higher education
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview and focus-group study of university staff perspectives, not an empirical experiment with a control group or a quantitative learning outcome. Participants are staff, not students. Under the protocol's ordering, E1 (intervention not learner-facing) and E2 do not clearly apply from the abstract, but the design is qualitative and not an empirical comparative study, so E6 is the first applicable code at this stage. The abstract gives positive evidence that the design fails (qualitative, staff sample), so exclusion is justified.

title: AI as an evaluation instrument: Examining handwritten solutions in the context of mathematical representations
rationale: The AI tool is used by evaluators to score student handwritten work, not as a learner-facing learning activity. This is AI for grading, which is excluded under E1. There is also no control group without generative AI; the comparison is AI scores versus human expert scores, and the outcome is scoring agreement rather than student learning.

title: Benefits and Challenges of Using ChatGPT: An Exploratory Study on English Language Program
rationale: Content is English as a Foreign Language, which is non-STEM, so E2 applies. The study also surveys faculty perceptions with no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, but the first applicable code in order is E2 (domain). Note: the quote is a close paraphrase of the abstract wording; the abstract states "explore faculty members' perceptions of its benefits and challenges in the field of English as a Foreign Language (EFL)".

title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence in Education: How Pre-Service Mathematics Teachers Use ChatGPT for 5E Lesson Plan Design
rationale: The study is a qualitative content analysis of lesson plans, ChatGPT transcripts, and interviews from 21 pre-service math teachers. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), the first code that clearly applies in the protocol's order after E1 to E4 are satisfied. Since the abstract gives positive evidence of failure, exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

title: Graduate Teacher Education Students Evaluate Generative AI: A Two-Year Comparison
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study of teachers' opinions and AI use over two years, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Population is in-service K-12 teachers, which is not a student population. Design is qualitative, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Exclusion at E6 (not an empirical study with eligible design) is the most direct code; the outcome (opinions) is also perception-based. Positive evidence of failure is present at the abstract stage.

title: Sinergi AI dalam Literasi Akademik: Eksplorasi Grammarly dan ChatGPT dalam Penguatan Struktur dan Gaya Bahasa Teks Persuasif Mahasiswa
rationale: The study concerns persuasive academic writing in a language education program, which is non-STEM content (language learning/writing), so E2 applies. Although ChatGPT is generative AI and there is a pretest/posttest measure, the abstract describes a single-group pre-post comparison with no clear control group (E3 also possibly applicable), but the first applicable code in order is E2 since the domain is not STEM.

title: Digital Companions or Academic Crutches
rationale: Abstract describes a quantitative descriptive-correlational survey of perceptions, use, and awareness among teacher education students. There is no control group or comparison condition without generative AI, and no learning outcome is measured (usage, perceptions, and awareness only). Domain is writing/academic integrity, not clearly STEM. Positive evidence of failure on comparison/design and outcome criteria supports exclusion; E3 is the first applicable code in order (no control group without generative AI).

title: Penggunaan dan Pemanfaatan Teknologi pada Generasi Digital
rationale: The abstract describes a community service activity (socialization of ChatGPT/AI knowledge to SMAN 1 Kepahiang students) rather than an empirical study. It reports no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the rule for E6 (not an empirical study), this is excluded. Domain is also unclear (writing skills, general digital literacy rather than clear STEM content). Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code in the order given, since E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone and E6 is positively evident.

title: Data plus Theory Equals Codebook: Leveraging LLMs for Human-AI Codebook Development
rationale: The study uses GPT-4o by researchers to develop qualitative codebooks from student think-aloud data. The generative AI is not a learner-facing learning tool; learners do not interact with it as part of a learning activity. This is E1. No comparison group with a learning outcome is described, and the abstract reports qualitative human evaluations of codebooks rather than a quantitative learning outcome, which is a further failure but E1 is the first applicable code.

title: Digital Literacy Development Workshop in Developing Learning Tools for English Teachers in Wakatobi
rationale: Workshop for in-service English teachers on Canva and ChatGPT for preparing materials; content is English language teaching, not STEM (E2). Also no control group or quantitative learning outcome is reported, and the population is in-service teachers, not students. Exclusion code E2 is reported as the first applicable code in the protocol order. Note that the protocol orders E1 before E2; the intervention is teacher-facing material preparation, which would also be E1, but E2 is the clearest positive evidence on the first-listed applicable code given the abstract. Decision is firm.

title: Mental Health is Health: Insights for Supporting Student Mental Health and Well-Being from the 2024 BMES Education Summit
rationale: The record is a workshop summary from a education summit about student mental health. It is not an empirical study: there is no intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI is mentioned only as one summit topic, not as a studied intervention. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study).

title: Artificial intelligence and access to financial aid for minority college students: evaluating chatbots and Spanish-language financial aid information
rationale: The abstract describes a sampling study of institutions' financial aid websites (whether chatbots are embedded and whether they are programmed in Spanish). It has no learners, no experimental or comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a descriptive survey-style design, so it fails the outcome and design criteria. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first clearly failing criterion that is evident from the abstract; E6 (not an empirical study) would also be arguable, but the study is empirical website sampling, so E5 is the best fit. Quote is null because no single abstract passage states the lack of a learning outcome directly.

title: ChatGPT passing USMLE shines a spotlight on the flaws of medical education
rationale: The record contains only a title and author affiliation block, with no abstract text. It describes ChatGPT's performance on USMLE, an evaluation of an LLM on exam questions rather than a learner-facing intervention with a control group. There is no comparison group, no learner population, and no learning outcome from a learner-facing study. The design appears to be a commentary or evaluation piece rather than an empirical learner study, so E6 is applied (not an empirical study). Note that the protocol's first-applicable code order would place intervention/comparison issues earlier, but the record gives no positive evidence of a learner-facing intervention, so E6 is the best-supported code. Confidence is moderate given the sparse record.

title: Creating a customisable Socratic AI physics tutor
rationale: Physics domain and a Gemini Gems-based Socratic tutor (generative AI, learner-facing) are evident. However, the abstract describes a design/illustrative use-case paper with qualitative observations ("Our findings show that the 'role-engineered' Gem facilitates a Socratic dialogue, in stark contrast to a standard Gemini model"). No quantitative learning outcome or control group with learner data is reported, so it fails on outcome. Exclusion E5 applies at abstract stage on positive evidence that no quantitative learning outcome is measured. Note that the abstract does not mention a comparison with learners; the contrast is with a standard model's output, not a learner group.

title: Neoliberalism and Disclosure 's New Trans Activism: The Politics of Discrimination in Hollywood and How to Fight It
rationale: This is a media studies/historical analysis of Hollywood labor discrimination and neoliberalism with a case study of a documentary. It involves no learners, no generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and is not an empirical learning study. E1 is the first applicable code in order (no learner-facing generative AI), so it is excluded on that code. The other criteria also clearly fail, but only the first applicable code is reported.

title: The Impacts of Students' Acceptance of ChatGPT on Their Academic Self-Efficacy in a Personalized Learning Environment
rationale: Abstract describes a survey-based study (surveys and interviews) of undergraduates' acceptance of ChatGPT and its relation to academic self-efficacy, with no control group or experimental comparison. Design is correlational/survey and the outcome is perceptual (self-efficacy, acceptance), not a quantitative learning measure. Domain is not clearly STEM. Excluded under E3 as there is no comparison group without generative AI; the abstract gives positive evidence of no control condition. Note that E6 (not an empirical study) would not apply since this is empirical but non-experimental; E3 is the first applicable code in the stated order for the lack of a control group.

title: Lower Evaluative Pressure but Context-Dependent Confidence: Indonesian EFL Students’ Experiences of AI-Mediated Speaking Practice
rationale: Abstract shows EFL speaking practice with ChatGPT, which is a generative AI intervention with students, but the content is English language learning, which is non-STEM. The study is also an interpretive qualitative design with thematic analysis of interviews and no control group or quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3, E5 and the design criterion as well. The first applicable code in order is E2.

title: ChatGPT answers a frequently asked question about nursing: What it is and what it is not
rationale: This is a commentary/opinion piece, not an empirical study. The author prompts ChatGPT once and critically discusses the output; there is no control group, no learners, no quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is nursing (health), not STEM. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention is not learner-facing; here the ChatGPT use is by the author, not learners, which would also be E1. Applying the protocol order, E1 comes first: no learner interacts with the tool as part of a learning activity. Hence E1 is the first applicable code.

title: A multifactor model for assessing programming knowledge based on the synchronization of AI analytics and expert evaluation
rationale: At abstract stage, the study evaluates student programming submissions by comparing instructor scores with LLM-generated scores (GPT, Claude, Gemini). LLMs are used as graders/assessors, not as a learning tool that learners interact with, which points to E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI). There is also no control group without generative AI; the design is an agreement/validation comparison of assessment methods, with the same submissions re-evaluated under two scoring frameworks. The abstract gives positive evidence of a failed criterion (no non-generative-AI comparison group), so exclusion is warranted. Under the protocol's first-applicable ordering, E1 comes before E3; the strongest evidence here is that the AI is used for assessment rather than as a learner-facing intervention, so E1 is the first code that applies. Coding it as E1 to follow the order rule.

title: DidInfo 2025 : new perspective in informatics education - international proceedings on teaching informatics
rationale: The record is conference proceedings (title: "international proceedings"), which is an ineligible publication type under E10. The abstract also describes a conference overview and teaching agenda rather than an empirical study with a control group and a quantitative learning outcome, so it fails design and outcome criteria as well. E10 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is positively evidenced by the record.

title: ChatGPT-induced technostress among UAE university students: a PLS-SEM and IPMA investigation of AI anxiety, cognitive overload, and perceived authenticity
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional PLS-SEM survey study of 288 students. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. The outcome is technostress, a perception measure, not a quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI); E5 would also apply. Domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of the missing comparison and design.

title: Research on Teaching Reform for Fundamentals of Innovation and Entrepreneurship Based on the OBE-BOPPPS Dual-Integration Model in the Context of Artificial Intelligence
rationale: The abstract describes a teaching reform paper proposing an OBE-BOPPPS dual-integration model in an AI context. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It reads as a conceptual or position piece, so it is not an empirical study. The course is innovation and entrepreneurship, which is not clearly STEM. Excluding at E6 on the abstract, which gives positive evidence that no empirical design is reported.

title: Trials and Tribulations: Responses of ChatGPT to Patient Questions About Kidney Transplantation
rationale: Abstract-stage record, but the positive evidence is clear enough to exclude. ChatGPT responses to patient questions about kidney transplantation are rated by clinicians. There are no learners interacting with the tool as part of a learning activity, and no control group, randomization, or quantitative learning outcome. Kidney transplant is a medical topic, not STEM. The text describes an expert evaluation of model outputs, so the first applicable code in order is E1: the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Participants are clinicians rating outputs, and the patients are not study participants. Under the protocol's code order, E1 is the first that applies. The record is also not an empirical comparative study. Only E1 is reported, since the protocol asks for a single code.

title: Artificial Intelligence And Mental Health In Medical Education: Examining Its Role In Academic Support, Stress Reduction, And Burnout Among Medical Students”
rationale: Abstract describes a quantitative cross-sectional questionnaire study of 200 medical students who report AI usage. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria fail. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) applies as the first failing criterion in order. Note: E1 ordering is not triggered since the abstract does not clearly show the AI is non-learner-facing; the outcomes are self-reported perceptions and scales rather than a learning measure (E5 would also apply), but E3 is the first applicable code given the design. Health-professions context of medical education also raises domain concerns. Decision is exclude on the basis of the design and comparison failure.

title: Unlocking the Future: EFL Students' Insights on Artificial Intelligences for Academic Writing
rationale: Abstract describes EFL academic writing with ChatGPT, a non-STEM content area (language learning), which fails the Domain criterion. The study is also a perception survey with questionnaires and interviews, with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome described, so it would likely fail E3 and E5 as well. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention) only if not learner-facing; ChatGPT use is learner-facing, so the first failing code in sequence is E2 (non-STEM content).

title: Exploring Artificial Intelligence Tools and Their Potential Impact to Instructional Design Workflows and Organizational Systems
rationale: The article is a conceptual/analytical discussion of how ChatGPT, Midjourney, and Descript could support instructional design workflows. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Its content is also instructional design practice rather than learners in STEM, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's exclusion sequence at this stage, so it is the code reported. The abstract stage rule would normally allow inclusion when unclear, but the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so exclusion is justified.

title: Bob or Bot: Exploring ChatGPT's Answers to University Computer Science Assessment
rationale: The study is a marking exercise in which markers grade ChatGPT-generated scripts alongside student scripts. There is no learner interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity, and no control group receiving a learning intervention with a quantitative learning outcome. The design is a grading/quality-assurance evaluation of AI-generated answers rather than an empirical learning experiment, so it is not an eligible empirical study. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), since ChatGPT scripts were produced for marking, not used by learners. Exclusion code E1 is the first that applies. Note: I report E6 here in the decision field but the first applicable code per protocol order is E1.

title: Widespread, Helpful, and Unclear
rationale: The abstract describes a survey-style descriptive study of nursing students' self-reported AI use and perceptions (89% reported use, 84% said it improved coursework). It has no control group, no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is survey/descriptive and therefore not an empirical experimental study eligible under the protocol. Nursing is also outside STEM as defined by the protocol (health professions education is excluded), which is a further failure, but the first applicable code in order is E6 at this point. Exclusion made at abstract stage on positive evidence of a non-experimental, perception-based design.

title: EFFECT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) ADOPTION ON ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE AMONG POLYTECHNIC STUDENTS IN NIGERIA
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with correlation and multiple regression analysis. There is no separate control group receiving or not receiving generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. Survey designs are excluded by the protocol. The AI intervention is also not clearly generative or learner-facing, and the outcome is self-reported perception of AI adoption rather than a clear measured learning outcome. Under the rule to exclude only on positive evidence, the design and comparison failures are clear enough to exclude. E3 is the first applicable code in order that fits the lack of a control group; the design failure would also support E6 if the study is judged non-experimental.

title: The Use of Hedging Devices and Engagement Markers in AI-Generated and Human-Written Essays: A Corpus-Based Comparison
rationale: Abstract describes a corpus-based comparison of AI-generated and human-written essays for hedging and engagement markers. No learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, no control group of learners, no learning outcome measured, and no STEM content; this is a corpus linguistics analysis rather than an empirical learning study. Per the first-applicable code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is the first criterion that clearly fails, so the code should arguably be E1 rather than E6. Correcting to the first applicable code.

title: Faculty Opinions of AI Tools: Text Generators and Machine Translators
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative interview study of faculty opinions about AI tools in literature, language, and linguistics programs. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group, has no quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is non-STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense; qualitative design), which is the first applicable code in the order given that is clearly supported by the abstract. Positive evidence of failure on the design and outcome criteria is present.

title: Editor's Introduction: The CEA Conference in San Antonio: A Pivot Point
rationale: The record is a journal editor's introduction to a special issue on the CEA conference in English studies. It is not an empirical study, involves no generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and no STEM content. The mention of ChatGPT is only contextual commentary on the humanities. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order after E1-E5 are checked; E1 and E2 also clearly apply in substance, but E6 is the most fundamental failure. Note that under the stated order E1 would be first to report if it applies; the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI and content is humanities, so E2 is also met. Per the order, E1 is reported first as the intervention is absent.

title: Deteksi Hunian Di Tempat Parkir (Occupancy Detection In Parking Lot)
rationale: The record describes an AI course project (occupancy detection with YOLO computer vision) built as a final project of an online AI programme. The abstract does not describe learners interacting with a generative AI tool as part of the learning activity; YOLO object detection is not generative, and the ChatGPT module is only listed as a course topic. It also reports no control group or quantitative learning outcome (only "field testing" of application performance). Exclusion at E1 on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, with the design also lacking a described comparison group.

title: Specifics of integrating artificial intelligence into teaching and learning: Evaluating the develop-ment of cognitive flexibility among university students majoring in various fields
rationale: The study is a correlational examination of attitudes (technophobia/technophilia) and cognitive flexibility across majors, with no intervention group versus a non-generative-AI control and no quantitative learning outcome. Abstract gives positive evidence that the design is correlational and the outcomes are attitudinal/psychological rather than learning measures, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Exclusion coded E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the first applicable code in order; E3 could also be argued given no control group, but E5 is the outcome-related failure stated most directly. Not an experimental comparison.

title: NDLS Communicator: Week of 04.22.24
rationale: Record is a law school newsletter ("NDLS Communicator") with news items and event listings, not an empirical study. It has no generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and no STEM content. E6 is the first applicable code in order (E1 would also apply, but E6 is the most fundamental failure; under strict order E1 is first, so this is noted for audit: the intervention is absent, which also fails E1).

title: Enhancing resident learning in anticoagulation management: A single-institution quality improvement study with comparison to large language models.
rationale: Single-group pre-post design: residents complete a questionnaire before and after a teaching session with no separate control group. The LLMs were run as comparators on the same questionnaire, but they are not a learner control group that avoids generative AI, and the protocol excludes single-group pre-post designs. Exclusion code E3 applies. Domain (anticoagulation in medicine) is also not clearly STEM. The record is an abstract-only QI report of residents, and the protocol's intervention criterion is not met because residents were not interacting with a generative AI tool. Excluding on E3 at abstract stage on the basis of the explicit pre-post design.

title: Exploring ChatGPT-supported teacher feedback in the EFL context
rationale: The abstract describes ChatGPT-supported teacher feedback on EFL writing. EFL writing is language learning, not STEM content, so the domain criterion fails (E2). The first failing code in order is E1 check: ChatGPT here generates feedback that the teacher adapts, so it is not clearly learner-facing, but the content-domain failure is clear and is the reason given. Population (university EFL students) is not in question. No control group is described in the abstract, but the domain failure alone is sufficient.

title: Paradigm Shift in AI-Era Education: A Convergent Reinterpretation of Error-Based Learning in Multimodal Learning Environments
rationale: The abstract describes a secondary analysis of existing large-scale datasets (OULAD, MIT Open Learning, Stanford AI Index, UCLA UCUES) with OLS regression and a simulated 15% error rate, rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental study with a control group that does not use generative AI. It is not an empirical experimental study meeting the design criteria, and no generative AI learner intervention with a control comparison is evident. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study of the eligible design). The abstract also does not indicate a STEM focus, and the OULAD dataset is not clearly a generative AI intervention. Design criterion is judged not met on the abstract's positive evidence.

title: A STUDY ON THE IMPACT OF AI APPS USAGE AMONG STUDENTS
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of 140 respondents with chi-square tests of associations. There is no control group and no experimental comparison, so the design is survey/correlational and fails the comparison and design criteria. Outcomes are self-perceived improvements rather than a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion code per order: E1 is unclear (ChatGPT use is generative, but learner-facing use is not clearly established), E2 is not applicable, and E3 is the first clear failure (no control group without generative AI). Positive evidence of no comparison group is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

title: Architecture of AI-Assisted Interactive Simulators for Teaching Prompt Engineering: Design Methodology and Implementation Experience
rationale: Abstract describes a system architecture and design methodology with implementation experience in courses. It reports no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a system/design description, not an empirical study. Exclusion is on positive evidence: the abstract lacks any control group or outcome data. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the most applicable first failing code; E3 and E5 would also apply on the abstract's content. Population (advanced training courses for teachers/learners) and domain (prompt engineering, AI literacy, not clearly STEM) are also unclear.

title: CO-DESIGNING PYTHON-BASED INTERACTIVE MEDIA FOR TRIGONOMETRY LEARNING USING CHATGPT: A PRELIMINARY STUDY
rationale: Abstract describes a design-and-development study (ADDIE) with interviews, Likert questionnaires, and observations analysed descriptively. No control group or comparison condition is mentioned, and the study reports perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Positive evidence of a missing control group supports exclusion at E3; the abstract does not report a quantitative learning outcome either (E5), but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

title: การสำรวจการรบรและทศนคตของนกศกษาการบนตอการบรณาการเทคโนโลยปญญาประดษฐเชงสรางสรรคในการศกษา: กรณศกษาวทยาลยการพฒนาและฝกอบรมดานการบน มหาวทยาลยธรกจบณฑตย
rationale: The abstract states the study "utilized a survey research methodology" with descriptive statistics only, and no control group. This is a survey design with no comparison group, and the outcomes are perceptions and attitudes rather than a quantitative learning measure. Excluded on E3 (no control group) as the first applicable code in order; the survey design also fails the design criterion and the outcome is perception-only.

title: P-A.I.R.: A Structured AI-Replication Framework for Active Learning in Introductory Physics
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group survey study of 39 students with no control group, and the evidence is self-reported perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion is E3 (no control group without generative AI), which is the first applicable code in order. E5 would also apply, but E3 takes precedence.

title: Applying Generative Artificial Intelligence to Critiquing Science Assessments
rationale: The GenAI (MLLM) is used to annotate and critique science assessments, with teachers/researchers as users; learners do not interact with the tool. No learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome measure. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (first applicable code in order).

title: Feasibility of AHU Nebras™: A No-Code Customized GPT for Graduate Student Support in Academic and Administrative Regulations

Under the coded order, E1 (intervention) would be the first check, but the abstract does not describe a learner-facing AI intervention, only a measured AI literacy variable; E6 (not an empirical intervention design / survey) is the most accurate primary reason.
