title: DTechCon Abstracts 2025
rationale: This record is a conference abstract compilation (DTechCon Abstracts 2025, International Journal of Diabetes and Technology) containing many short abstracts, not a journal article. It covers diabetes care (health domain, not STEM education) and patients with type 2 diabetes rather than students. The abstracts do not describe learners interacting with generative AI in a learning activity. Under the protocol, conference proceedings/abstract-only records are publication-type ineligible (E10), but the protocol's E10 code applies to conference proceedings; the record is an abstract collection, so E10 is the most fitting code. Note: the first-applicable code ordering is E1 (intervention not learner-facing genAI) first; the abstracts include a generative AI tool (DiaShield X using ChatGPT-4) used by clinicians, not learners, which is E1 applicable. Choosing E1 as the first applicable code in protocol order.

title: VIDEO-BASED LEARNING IN THE DIGITAL AGE: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES
rationale: The abstract describes a literature review, policy analysis, and a questionnaire survey of 67 people. It is not an experimental study with a control group and reports no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical comparative study. Video-based learning is not a generative AI intervention with a control arm, and the domain is not clearly STEM. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in this design-based assessment; the survey is descriptive and not a randomized or quasi-experimental design.

title: Introduction to the Special Section on Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in Learning Design: An Editorial with a Commentary
rationale: The record is an editorial introducing a special section of design cases. It is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also reports no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome. Under the abstract rule, the exclusion rests on the positive evidence that the record is an editorial.

title: Human-Technology Interactions in Vocational Training: Insights from Italian Craft and Industrial Education
rationale: The abstract describes an observational questionnaire study of student perceptions about craft careers, with subgroup comparisons only. It involves no learner interaction with a generative AI tool, no control group, no learning outcome, and no experimental design. Generative AI appears only as an LLM-assisted survey analysis workflow by researchers, and VR/AI recommendation systems are mentioned only as design implications. Exclusion at the first applicable code: E1 would also fit, since AI is used only by researchers, but the study is clearly non-empirical in the trial sense and is observational, so E6 is the most direct code. Note the protocol's E1 applies first in order; given the first applicable code in order is E1 (AI used only by researchers, not learner-facing), the code should be E1.

title: The impact of Gen AI on art and design program education
rationale: Abstract describes Gen AI in art and design education. Art and design is not one of the protocol's STEM domains (science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science), so the content criterion fails. The abstract also gives no indication of a control group, a learning outcome measure, or a comparative quantitative design, but the domain failure alone is sufficient. Exclude at E2, the first applicable code in order.

title: The Signals That Matter: Resumes, Cover Letters, and Success on the Job Search
rationale: The study observes job applicants' resumes and cover letters and their job-search outcomes. No learner interacts with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; ChatGPT is mentioned only as a speculative future source of document features. Not a learning intervention, not STEM content, and the design is observational rather than an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison with a control group. Excluded at the first applicable code, E1.

title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE TEACHING PROCESS
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical and demonstrative article with code examples and recommended methods. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no learning outcome data, so it does not appear to be an empirical study. Positive evidence of a failing criterion (no empirical design or outcome) is present, so exclusion under E6 is supported. Programming domain is STEM and the year is 2025.

title: INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL GENERATIVA COMO FERRAMENTA DE APOIO À PRÁTICA DOCENTE: RELATO DE EXPERIÊNCIA NO ENSINO DE INFORMÁTICA E ROBÓTICA NO ENSINO FUNDAMENTAL
rationale: The study is a qualitative, reflective experience report by a teacher about AI use in lesson planning. It is not an empirical comparative study: there is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The generative AI is used by the teacher, not learners (E1 also applies), but the first applicable code in the order given is E1. Correction: the intervention is teacher-facing only, so E1 is the first applicable code and should be used instead of E6.

title: INVESTIGATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES IN GENERATING LVAR
rationale: Abstract describes generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Leonardo.AI, Lumen5.AI, Pictory.AI) used to create Linking Visual Active Representations, and an educational experiment. However, the abstract describes content analysis of a ChatGPT dialogue and a qualitative-style evaluation through Bloom's taxonomy; it reports no quantitative learning outcome, no control group, and no effect data. Positive evidence of a missing quantitative outcome is present, so exclusion under E5 is applied. Not clearly STEM either, but E5 is the first applicable code in the order given at abstract stage based on the evidence available. The "experiment" wording is not enough to show a control group or quantitative measure.

title: Investigating pre-service teachers’ AI literacy for ELL instruction: A mixed-methods study
rationale: Study concerns pre-service teachers' AI literacy for ELL (English language learner) instruction, a language-teaching context rather than STEM content. The design appears to be a single-group pre-post comparison ("before and after two interventions"), with no control group described, which would also fail E3. Excluded under E2 as the first applicable code, per the ordering. Quote is null because the abstract supports the content judgment only indirectly.

title: How Data Analytics Can Be Leveraged to Enhance Graduate Clinical Skills Education
rationale: The record is a perspective piece, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no learning outcome data. Generative AI is discussed only in general terms, and the domain is clinical/medical education rather than STEM. E6 is the first code that applies in the protocol's order, so it is reported.

title: Pressure to Plagiarize and the Choice to Cheat: Toward a Pragmatic Reframing of the Ethics of Academic Integrity
rationale: This is a philosophical/conceptual argument paper using case studies, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, comparison group, or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Generative AI is mentioned only as context.

title: Determinants of Students’ Academic Honesty in the Context of AI-Based Learning Tools
rationale: The abstract describes a survey-based SEM study of psychological determinants (Theory of Planned Behavior) of academic honesty. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome; it is a correlational/survey design, not an experiment. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study is too loose here), but the design is clearly non-experimental and the outcome is behavioral intention, not learning. Code chosen as the first applicable: E1 would also apply since AI tools are only mentioned as context, not as an intervention learners interact with in a learning activity. Given the rule that the first applicable code is reported in order, E1 is the earliest code that applies on the abstract's evidence and should be preferred.

title: Prevalence of artificial intelligence use and instruction in nursing education: A national study of prelicensure nursing programs in the United States
rationale: The record is a national prevalence study of AI use and instruction in prelicensure nursing programs, which is a survey-type design. It reports no learner-facing intervention with a comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Nursing is also a health professions domain, which the protocol excludes. The abstract is missing, but the title alone indicates a non-experimental prevalence study, so it is excluded as not an empirical intervention study. Exclusion code E6 is used because it is a survey (non-experimental) design, which fails the design criterion. Note that the protocol's domain exclusion for health professions education would also apply.

title: Percepción y usos de la IA en estudiantes del área computacional: un estudio descriptivo
rationale: Descriptive questionnaire study of 190 computer science students' uses and perceptions of generative AI. No control group and no comparison design; not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Outcomes are perceptions and usage, not a quantitative learning measure. Code E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order at abstract stage (no control group without generative AI), though E6 (non-empirical/descriptive survey) would also apply; the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group.

title: Strengthening the Technological Literacy of Teachers at SMPN 2 Baturraden through Generative AI Training for Teaching Material Development
rationale: This is a community service training for in-service teachers using generative AI to build teaching materials. The AI is used by teachers, not learner-facing, so E1 applies. The abstract also reports only satisfaction, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, and the participants are in-service teachers, which is outside the population criteria. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

title: AI-Assisted Rubric-Based Essay Grading in Dental Hygiene Education: A retrospective observational study.
rationale: Title describes a dental hygiene education study on AI-assisted essay grading. Dental hygiene is a health professions field, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain, and the AI is used for grading rather than as a learner-facing tool. Design is described as retrospective observational, which is not a randomized or comparison-group quasi-experiment. No abstract is available. Excluded on E2 as the first applicable code in order, with the domain failure as the clearest positive evidence. Note that E1 (AI used for grading, not learner-facing) would also plausibly apply.

title: Телеологічні та некоректні причинні пояснення у шкільних підручниках з біології: потенційні ризики для формування наукового мислення учнів
rationale: The study is a content analysis of school biology textbooks. The large language model was used only to screen textbook text for the researchers, not as a learner-facing intervention (E1 would apply), and there is no control group or learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1, but the clearest failure is that it is not an empirical experiment; the abstract gives positive evidence of a textbook content analysis with no learner interaction with generative AI. Coding it E6 as not an empirical study of the protocol's kind; no learner-facing generative AI, no comparison, no outcome.

title: Insights of higher-level educators on integrating AI technology into their teaching practices
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study based on interviews with tertiary educators, not an empirical controlled study with a comparison group or quantitative learning outcome. Participants are educators rather than students, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the primary reason under the protocol's order; the study is qualitative, which fails the design criterion, and the outcome criterion is also not met.

title: Enhancing human-AI communication in language education: Developing customized chatbots for teaching genre analysis and annotation
rationale: Abstract shows the content is English for Research Publication Purposes / genre analysis, a language-education topic rather than STEM, so E2 applies first. The study also reports chat histories and questionnaires with eleven doctoral students and no control group or quantitative learning outcome, so E3 and E5 would also likely apply, but E2 is the first code in order.

title: OI-Assistant: A Retrieval Augmented System for Similar Problem Discovery and Interactive Learning in Competitive Programming
rationale: The tool is a RAG/LLM system used by competitive programming students (STEM, higher/secondary learners). However, the abstract reports only student feedback and ratings of helpfulness and preliminary search-precision tests, with no described randomized or quasi-experimental control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failing the comparison criterion is lacking at abstract stage strictly, but the comparisons described (feedback ratings, search results) do not indicate a learning-outcome control group. Excluding on E3 as the most likely failure: the abstract describes no control group using non-generative AI learning conditions, only perception-based comparisons to traditional OJs and ChatGPT. Note that the outcome criterion (E5) would also plausibly apply since only perceptions and retrieval precision are reported.

title: Исследовательское обучение как метод фундаментальной математической подготовки студентов STEM-направлений в условиях цифровой трансформации образования
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual model and a diagnostic attitude questionnaire administered to first-year STEM students. It reports no control group and no comparison design, and the only measured outcome is perception of mathematics (affective), not a learning outcome. There is positive evidence of failure on comparison/design (no control group mentioned, descriptive survey) and outcome. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI), so E3 is reported. E5 would also apply. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence.

title: LLM-Based Clinical History Taking System: A Persona-Driven Approach
rationale: The study concerns clinical history-taking training with LLM-generated standardized patients, which is health professions education and therefore non-STEM under the protocol's domain exclusion. The abstract also reports only expert ratings and student perceptions (appropriateness, accuracy ratings), with no quantitative learning outcome and no control group. Exclusion uses the first applicable code, E2, since the domain check comes before the outcome and comparison checks.

title: From lectures to learning outcomes: meaningful integration of AI-generated content in pre-clerkship medical training
rationale: Pre-clerkship medical training (genetics and pharmacology blocks) with LLM-generated summaries and flashcards. Medical education is a health professions context, which the protocol excludes from the domain criterion (health professions education is not STEM). Exclude at E2. Medical students are higher-education learners, so population is not the failing criterion. Design is unclear from the abstract (self-selected AI use with baseline comparison and difference-in-differences), but the domain failure is sufficient for exclusion.

title: From computer-supported collaborative learning to human–AI collaboration: CSCL research in fifty years of Computers & Education
rationale: The record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. The title indicates a review-style retrospective of CSCL research in a journal over fifty years ("CSCL research in fifty years of Computers & Education"), which is not an empirical study. This is positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so E6 applies. No quote is available since the abstract is absent.

title: Building foundations for independent clinical reasoning in an AI era: Student experiences with the independent authentic clinical reasoning task in prelicensure nursing education
rationale: The record is a prelicensure nursing education study on clinical reasoning. Nursing/health professions education is excluded from the STEM domain by protocol (Domain: exclude health professions education), so the record fails the domain criterion. No abstract is available, but the title alone gives positive evidence of a health professions context. Exclusion code E2 applies. Other criteria cannot be assessed from the title alone.

title: Addressing a Bias in Evaluating of Student Self-Explanations of Worked Programming Examples
rationale: The abstract describes a comparison of explanation-assessment approaches (semantic similarity versus LLM prompting) on a previously published dataset of student explanations. It does not describe a learner-facing intervention with a control group, a learning outcome, or an experimental design. This appears to be a computational evaluation of assessment methods rather than an empirical learning study, so E6 applies. Venue is a conference-style outlet (Florida AI Research Society), which may also raise E10, but the first applicable code in order is E6 on the abstract evidence. Note the record is excluded on positive evidence of a non-experimental design, not on missing information.

title: AI literacy: A core practice in world language education
Comparative Impact of ChatGPT and Conventional Search Tools on Clinical Reasoning Performance: A Randomized Crossover Study in Preclinical Medical Students [Letter]
rationale: The record is a letter to the editor commenting on a randomized crossover study, not an empirical study itself. It reports no original data for the authors' own experiment. The abstract text is a set of critical comments referring to the original study (n=46 preclinical medical students, ChatGPT vs conventional search, eight-point rubric). Under the protocol, a letter/commentary is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Publication type is also arguably not a journal research article, but E6 is the first applicable code in order. Population and the general topic appear to fit, but the record is not itself an eligible study. Note that the domain (clinical reasoning in medicine) may also raise E2 concerns, but E6 is reported as the first applicable code.

title: Birds of a feather: clustering mental models to explore how people think alike
rationale: Abstract describes a method that uses generative AI and network science to analyze students' textual mental models about ChatGPT, with validation against self-reported survey data. There is no learning intervention with a control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the study is a methods/elicitation study. Survey perceptions are not learning outcomes. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first applicable code in the order; E5 would also plausibly apply. Note that the first applicable code in order is E1 if the AI is not learner-facing, which is unclear here, so E3 is the best fit for the stated design.

title: Embracing the Future of Distance Science Education: Opportunities and Challenges of ChatGPT Integration
rationale: The abstract describes an illustrative, non-empirical exposition of ChatGPT uses in distance education. It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; outputs are evaluated qualitatively. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies (first applicable code in the order given, since E1-E5 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract alone and E6 is the clear positive failure).

title: Caring Too Much? Emotional Labor and Compassion Fatigue among Faculty during the COVID-19 Pandemic
rationale: The record is a qualitative study of faculty emotional labor and compassion fatigue. It involves no generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM content, and no quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in protocol order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), since no generative AI tool appears in the abstract. However, the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative, non-empirical-quantitative design, so E6 is recorded as the most fitting code. Note: under strict code order E1 would apply first; the auditor should review this choice.

title: Beyond ChatGMP: Improving LLM generation through user preferences
rationale: The abstract describes a proof-of-concept ILASP system learning user preferences to tailor LLM output. It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; the work appears to be a method/proof of concept rather than an empirical learning study. Exclude under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) on positive evidence from the abstract. The domain (interview exercise) is not clearly STEM either, but E5 is the clearest failure and is applied as the first failing code in the abstract.

title: Improving L2 vocabulary retention and learning engagement through L1 traditional stories in review activities using ChatGPT-generated questions
rationale: The study targets L2 (second language) vocabulary learning, which is language learning and not STEM content. Although participants are computer science freshmen, the content taught is English vocabulary, so the domain criterion fails (E2). Also, ChatGPT is used by the teacher to generate review questions, which would be E1 for the intervention since learners do not interact with the generative AI tool directly. E2 is reported as the first applicable code in protocol order.

title: The Analysis of the Misuse of the Quantifier “Ge”
rationale: The paper concerns the misuse of the Chinese quantifier "Ge" by international learners, a Chinese language topic rather than STEM. Protocol excludes language learning and other non-STEM content (E2), which is the first applicable code in order. The abstract also describes a conceptual/proposal paper with no control group or quantitative learning outcome, and ChatGPT is only mentioned as a suggestion, so further codes would apply, but E2 is the first that applies.

title: Analysis of Student Experience in Using Building Information Modeling (BIM) to Understand the Concept of Steel Structure
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study with thematic analysis of interviews with 10 students, with no separate control group. This is a qualitative design lacking a comparison group, which fails the comparison and design criteria. Although BIM is not clearly generative AI, the decisive failure is the absence of a control group (E3). Using the abstract-stage rule, exclusion is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison. Note that the rule to exclude only on positive evidence is met here, since the abstract explicitly states a qualitative approach and interviews only.

title: The Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence in South African Law Libraries: The Role of a Law Librarian
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative, conceptual review with no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study in the protocol sense. Domain is legal research, not STEM, and participants are law librarians/practitioners rather than students. E6 is the first applicable code in order at the abstract stage given the non-empirical design; the abstract gives positive evidence of this failure.

title: Designing a Digital Learning Ecosystem based on Gallery Walk with Virtual Board Technology
rationale: This is an editorial-style letter describing a faculty workshop built on Miro virtual boards and a Gallery Walk. It involves no generative AI as a learner-facing intervention (AI tools were only mentioned as used in article writing). The outcome is satisfaction and perceptions from 22 faculty participants, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code is E1, as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Participants are also faculty, not students. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because positive evidence of failure is present.

title: Pelatihan Penyusunan Bahan Ajar dan Asesmen Interaktif Bermuatan Kearifan Lokal Melalui AI Untuk Meningkatkan Literasi Digital Guru SD
rationale: Community service training program for elementary teachers (in-service), using ChatGPT and other AI tools to build materials. The abstract describes a single-group training with pre/post-style improvement and survey perceptions; no control group. Population is in-service teachers, which is excluded, and design lacks a comparison group. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code on the protocol's ordering that is clearly supported; E4 (in-service teachers) also applies but E3 is listed first in the order used here.

title: Approach with Caution: An Innovative Educator Reviews the Impact AI Could Have on Education
rationale: The abstract describes an opinion/reflective article by the author exploring ChatGPT. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the design is non-empirical.

title: Optimization of Prompt Engineering in the Development of Intelligent Tutor Chatbots for Personalized Learning
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It reports no primary experimental comparison or quantitative learning outcome, and there is no control group. Other criteria are not assessable from the abstract, but the E6 failure alone is sufficient for exclusion.

title: Research on Key Technologies of Adaptive Teaching Based on Student Digital Profiles—Student, Team, and Role Profiling Models for Process Evaluation in Project-Based Learning
rationale: Abstract describes a learning analytics/profiling framework for process evaluation of 165 students with no described control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome measured against a control. The design appears to be a descriptive system development study. Per the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is uncertain because the LLM generates teacher diagnostics rather than learner interaction, but the clearest failing criterion is the absence of a control group (E3). Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of no comparison group.

title: Advanced Question Answer Generation (QAG) for mastering vocabulary proficiency using Generative AI
rationale: The study evaluates Llama 3 for generating SAT Words-in-Context questions. The content is English vocabulary/reading and writing, which is not STEM (protocol excludes language and non-STEM content). The abstract also reports model accuracy on generated questions, not a learner outcome, and reports no control group with learners. Excluded on E2, the first applicable code in order-of-check terms; the abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM content.

title: WEBQUESTS AS AN INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGY FOR PROFESSIONALLY-ORIENTED FOREIGN LANGUAGE TEACHING
rationale: The study addresses professionally-oriented foreign language teaching (English for computer science). Content is foreign language learning, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM. The abstract also gives no evidence of a control group or a quantitative learning outcome, and generative AI is only mentioned as a prospect. E2 is the first applicable code in order, so the record is excluded on domain.

title: Comparative analysis of multi-criteria decision making methods for prioritizing influential factors of ChatGPT adoption in higher education
rationale: The record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. The title indicates a multi-criteria decision making study of influential factors of ChatGPT adoption, which points to adoption perceptions rather than a quantitative learning outcome. The title gives positive evidence that the study prioritizes adoption factors via MCDM methods, not a controlled comparison measuring learning, so the outcome criterion appears to fail. Confidence is limited because the abstract is missing. Under the abstract-stage rule this should arguably be "unsure" rather than excluded, since the title alone does not fully establish the absence of a learning outcome.

title: Вплив діджиталізації на спектр вмінь англомовної компетентності студентів закладів вищої освіти в рамках професійної підготовки
rationale: The title (Ukrainian) and the supplied text concern English-language competence of university students, which is language learning and not STEM, so the domain criterion fails. The supplied "abstract" is actually a reference list with no study design, intervention, comparison, or outcome described. Domain failure is positive evidence, so exclude under E2. Note that the record also lacks any evidence of a generative AI intervention or a control group.

title: Predicting learning depth through dialogue : A design-based approach to SOLO classification using Naive Bayes in online MBA education
rationale: The study is a Naive Bayes classifier predicting SOLO levels from coded forum posts, with no described control group or comparison condition without generative AI. The abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group (single-cohort design across three instructional cycles). The AI element is ChatGPT-facilitated prompts mentioned only in findings, and the domain is MBA (business), which is not STEM, so E2 could also apply. Exclude under E3 as the first applicable code, since the comparison criterion fails on positive evidence.

title: SCIENCE STUDENTS AWARENESS AND PERCEPTION OF USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TOOLS IN AMINU SALEH COLLEGE OF EDUCATION, BAUCHI STATE
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey with no learner intervention and no control group; it measures awareness and perceptions only, with no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical experimental study meeting the design criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the study is a survey, which falls under the protocol's non-eligible designs; the first-applicable code by order would be E1 given the intervention is not described as a learner-facing generative AI activity, but the abstract gives no evidence of a learning activity, so E6 best reflects the survey design. Survey-only perception data also fail the outcome criterion.

title: Nexus Point: The Tech & Strategy Hub
rationale: The record is a conference/event program description for a technology showcase with product demo booths, not an empirical study. It reports no comparison group, no design, and no learning outcome. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6); publication type (E10) would also apply given it is a program listing rather than a journal article.

title: Learning Tools Using ChatGPT in the Biochemistry Class: Creating Notes and Performance on Exams
rationale: The abstract describes students using ChatGPT-generated study materials and ChatGPT being run on past exams, with no separate control group of students who do not use generative AI. Student perception results are not a learning-outcome comparison, and the ChatGPT exam performance is not a learner comparison. There is no positive evidence of a control group, so the comparison criterion fails; the first failing code is E3. Biochemistry is STEM, so the domain criterion is met.

title: Exploring AI Acceptance in Higher Education Data Analytics for Accounting and Auditing: A TAM-Driven PLS-SEM Analysis
rationale: The study is a TAM-based PLS-SEM survey of students' acceptance and usage intention of AI. It has no control group and no learning outcome measure; it measures perceptions and intentions only, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Design is survey (not an experiment), which also fails the design criterion. Domain is accounting/auditing data analytics, which is borderline for STEM. Abstract evidence is sufficient to exclude on E5.

title: Transplantation & Tissue Engineering
rationale: The record is a withdrawn-titled, multi-abstract compilation from a transplant surgery journal's issue page (Journal of the American College of Surgeons). The abstracts concern transplant surgery, immunology, cost analysis, and survival outcomes in mice and patients. None describe learners interacting with a generative AI tool, and none concern STEM education. The record fails the intervention and domain criteria on the face of the text. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), which is checked before E2. The record would be E1 under strict code ordering, so the code should be read as E1 rather than E2. No quote is available because no passage refers to generative AI or learners.

title: AI-Enhanced Quality of Multimodal Physics Word Problems in Authentic Contexts Using the P-MAGIC App
rationale: Study is a physics (STEM) app using GPT-4o to generate problems, but the abstract reports evaluation of question quality by automatic and human (teacher) ratings. No quantitative learning outcome from students is described; "conceptual understanding" is asserted without a measured student outcome, and no control group is mentioned. Positive evidence of no learning outcome supports E5 at abstract stage. Note: the protocol's first-applicable ordering would place E1/E3 only if clearly shown; E5 is the clearest failing criterion here.

title: Graduate Students' Perceptions of Generative AI's Impact on Critical Thinking Development
rationale: The study is a survey of perceptions with no control group and no experimental comparison, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Outcomes are perceptions and usage, not a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first applicable code under the protocol's order would be E1 or E5; however, the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design, which is non-experimental. Per the rule of reporting the first applicable code, E1 is not clearly established (the intervention is not described as a learner-facing tool used in a learning activity), and E5 applies because the only outcomes are perceptions and usage. Final code chosen is E5 for the absence of a quantitative learning outcome.

title: From hype to insight: Exploring ChatGPT 's early footprint in education via altmetrics and bibliometrics
rationale: This is a bibliometric and altmetric analysis of publications about ChatGPT in education. It is not an empirical study of learners interacting with a generative AI tool, has no control group, and reports no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Under the protocol's code order, E1 would be the first applicable check, but the record does not describe a learner-facing intervention at all, so E6 is the most accurate code.

title: Metacognición digital: autorregulación del aprendizaje mediante IA
rationale: The abstract describes a systematic literature review, not an empirical study with a control group. The review's pooled percentages (e.g., 25%, 35%) do not come from a primary comparative design, so the record is not an empirical study and fails E6. The review nature is positive evidence at abstract stage, so exclusion is justified despite the abstract's ambiguity. Population (secondary education) and date (2024) are consistent with the protocol. Note that the abstract also mentions algebra and statistics, which would meet domain.

title: USE OF AI TOOLS IN DEVELOPING RESEARCH PROPOSALS AMONG PRE-SERVICE SCIENCE TEACHERS: A CASE STUDY
rationale: The abstract describes a case study with a mixed-methods questionnaire of pre-service science teachers using ChatGPT. There is no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. The design is descriptive (case study, questionnaire), not an experiment or quasi-experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported (only usage patterns and perceptions).
